scope: Convexity of substitution through arbitrary convex nonnegative coordinates into a head convex and monotone on the nonnegative orthant; specialization to positive/negative parts of raw inputs. No raw-input monotonicity or output nonnegativity is asserted by these two theorems.
semantic_findings: The incoming coordinate functions need convexity and nonnegativity, with no incoming monotonicity assumption.
Both points at which the outer monotonicity comparison is applied are proved to lie in the nonnegative orthant.
The ambient source domain is explicitly convex, ensuring the mixed input is in-domain.
The raw-input specialization uses max(x_i,0) and max(-x_i,0), both convex and nonnegative; no claim that both are monotone in x_i.
A documentation overstatement about output nonnegativity was corrected; theorem statements and proof terms were unchanged, and the final documented source rebuilt successfully.
boundary_checks: A one-coordinate sum head gives the convex absolute-value raw-input pullback.
Negative-part input coordinate is explicitly shown not to be monotone on all real inputs.
